consensus_summary: Primary identification is Satan (the devil/ancient serpent), settled by Revelation’s explicit equations; common alternatives are hostile empires/rulers (Egypt, Babylon, Rome), primordial chaos monsters (Leviathan/Rahab/tannin), and rarer symbolic or literal-creature readings.
book_summary: The dragon is defined as a devouring kingdom, illustrated by Pharaoh/Egypt and Babylon/Nebuchadnezzar.
boundary_disagreement: Consensus centers Satan for the principal NT texts and treats OT political dragons as secondary/background or typological; the book makes the political/devouring-kingdom sense the core definition and relegates the Satan reading to a noted but non-adopted common teaching.
material_contradiction: Consensus primary referent (Satan) is replaced by the book’s primary referent (devouring kingdom); both cannot be the core identification of the same symbol in the same sense.
rationale: All three consensus responses treat Satan as the settled primary meaning on the strength of Revelation 12:9 and 20:2, while listing devouring kingdoms/empires among the alternatives. The book’s entry states only “A devouring kingdom,” supplies solely the OT empire citations, and flags the Satan view merely as “commonly taught.” This substitutes a different core referent rather than narrowing, broadening, or rewording the consensus core, even though the book’s examples appear among consensus alternatives.
strongest_objection: Revelation 12:9 and 20:2 explicitly name the dragon Satan, which the consensus rightly takes as definitive for the dominant biblical usage; the OT kingdom metaphors, while real, are secondary and do not override that identification.
